problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}-2 & -4 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & -4 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{33}$ equal to zero.*

activity_context.topic_title: Finding Determinants Using Row and Column Operations

feedback.problem:
Calculate the value of 
$\,|\begin{aligned}5 & -8 & 3 & -2 \\ -7 & 5 & -4 & -1 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 & 2 \\ -6 & -4 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}|.$

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{33}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4\times 4$ determinant to a $3\times 3$ determinant.*
feedback.worked_solution:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{33}=1$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}5 & -8 & 3 & -2 \\ -7 & 5 & -4 & -1 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 & 2 \\ -6 & -4 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+(-3){C}_{3} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+{C}_{3} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+(-2){C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-4 & -5 & 3 & -8 \\ 5 & 1 & -4 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-4 & -5 & 3 & -8 \\ 5 & 1 & -4 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}-4 & -5 & -8 \\ 5 & 1 & 7 \\ 0 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-4 & -5 & -8 \\ 5 & 1 & 7 \\ 0 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-6)\cdot (-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}-4 & -8 \\ 5 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =6(-28+40) \\  & =72.\end{aligned}
$$
